For me this is better for L4D, it's just sad that the developers abandoned this game:(. Hoping to have L4D3 soon.

[h1] The Privacy Policy concerns are unfounded and are frankly just paranoid. [/h1]

[h2] As a previous reviewer pointed out, the Privacy Policy contains a few things that may raise a few eyebrows, such as: [/h2]

[i] Account and Contact Information:
Name, phone number, postal address, email address, username, password, age, or birth date.

Payment, Purchase and Account Information:
Credit, debit or other payment card information and Information about your subscription, account, purchases, or discounts.

Photos, Videos, or Audio Information:
Images or recordings from your device or that you otherwise post or submit to us or photos or recordings of you from live experiences or events.

Usage and Viewing Information:
Films, TV shows, and videos that you view (including title and genre, watchlists you compile, and searches you conduct), webpages, apps, and ads you see and interact with, as well as the accounts you link together, including recordings of your interactions with our Services, which may include mouse clicks, mouse movements, keystrokes, and page scrolling. When you use our Service, you consent to the recording of your interactions with us. [/i]

[b] However, [/b] this privacy policy applies to [u] Warner Brothers as a company as an entity [/u] - not exclusive to the game. These requirements to the privacy policy make sense when you consider that Warner Bros. has a [i] Streaming service [/i]. Which would absolutely track all of those things as a industry standard. (Not agreeing with the practice, but I can't argue it isn't standard practice.)

In nowhere in the games EULA does it make any mention of this kind of monitoring. If you're afraid of them spying on you, please understand that by owning [b] STEAM [/b] you already are giving up this information.
